key_insight: A strong drive on far-detuned fixed-frequency transmons can generate a large XX-YY interaction, enabling a fast ZZ-free bSWAP gate with tunable phase control.
engineering_relevance: This provides an alternative to cross-resonance for gate synthesis, with better SWAP efficiency and a path to improved two-qubit operations in spectrally crowded superconducting processors.
method: Apply a single strong drive to induce the XX-YY coupling in the far-detuned regime.
Use a weak second tone to compensate and tune away the unwanted ZZ interaction.
Demonstrate a 150-ns sqrt(bSWAP) gate and two-spin squeezing via two-axis countertwisting.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct experimental implementation and comparison on the same qubit pair, showing faster SWAP and higher IRB fidelity for sqrt(bSWAP), plus a multilevel-theory prediction of a stronger-drive CNOT advantage.
watch_item: The approach relies on careful multi-tone calibration and strong-driving conditions, so performance may depend sensitively on device-specific multilevel dynamics and drive-induced errors.
paper_title: ZZ-Free bSWAP Gates under Strong Driving in Far-Detuned Fixed-Frequency Transmons
